source: W3C ODRL CG formal-semantics examples C2 (C21, C22, C23)
notes: Translated from the W3C ODRL CG formal-semantics examples (w3c/odrl@1db8e6b, folder C Evaluation of Conditions (Duties)/C2). The CG's evaluatedAction/Target/Party become the request; requestParameters describing sotw:CurrentXSDDateTime become request.at and effective_at (odrl:dateTime is the action time in due2-core). The CG reports a controlState: Inactive is Deny under its default 'close' behaviour, where due2 says NotApplicable and leaves the default to the enforcement point. Timezone-less instants are read as UTC (due2 instants are UTC, workflows §2). Upstream defect: every CG request in C1/C2 names ex:party/billie1, but the policy's assignee is ex:party/billie, and the CG's expected reports treat the request as matching (C12, C23 Permit). The translation uses ex:party/billie; read literally, every C scenario would be NotApplicable. The duty's own constraint (Sunday) is a guard: it reads the request, so it decides whether the duty is owed (workflows §5.2, `owed`). The CG agrees: C21 reports the duty Inactive and the permission Active. Guards stay on the duty (decisions/0003), so the policy is one permission atom and one duty atom. 2025-07-29 is a Tuesday, 2025-08-03 a Sunday; the weekday is a request parameter the assembler derives from request.at (due2-profiles.md §3, one hop). Scenarios 4-5 are added and cover an unknown guard. It is uniform — a positive occurrence only lowers the verdict — so the two extreme completions decide (k = 0). Until decisions/0003 this case was the motivating case for canonical literals, because hoisting split the guard into complementary atoms; that role has passed to due2-xone-unknown. odrl:payAmount needs no binding in the policy: due2-core binds it to the witness source, so the CG's policy is used as written (due2-profiles.md §9 #6). The CG's refinement states odrl:unit Euro, a unit due2-core's odrl:payAmount does not declare (currencies vary), so W1 admits the policy with the warning UncheckedUnit and the witness condition is U with status misfit whatever amount a payment states (decisions/0049): a value with no stated unit cannot be checked against 5.00 EUR. A scenario whose duty a payment would fulfil is therefore Indeterminate between Pending and Permit where the CG answers Permit. A policy that needs the amount checked binds an operand of its own that declares due2:unit.

expected.why: The guard is F, so the duty is not owed and is not open; ex:rule/C2 applies and is ready.
The guard is T, so the duty is owed, and it has no witness: open, outstanding. One route: pay.

The guard is T, so the duty is owed. ev-pay is a timely compensate by the bearer, but the refinement's unit Euro is one odrl:payAmount's binding does not declare, so the payAmount condition is U (misfit) and fulfilled is U: Permit where the payment counts, Pending where it does not. Indeterminate, Pending..Permit.

The weekday is missing, so owed is U, and the unchecked unit makes fulfilled U, so open (owed ∧ ¬fulfilled) is U: completing it F gives a ready candidate (Permit), T a pending one (Pending). Indeterminate, Pending..Permit.

owed is U and the duty is unfulfilled, so open is U: completing owed F gives a ready candidate (Permit), owed T a pending one (Pending). The completions disagree: Indeterminate, exact. The authored policy is undecided too — Sunday would be Pending, any other day Permit.
